text: The warehouse is already running when marketing comes back with a new question: why do customers actually place their orders? AdventureWorks2012 already has a real answer, in two tables this capstone hasn't touched yet.

Grouping the real bridge table by order ID and filtering for more than one row proves the problem: plenty of real orders have more than one sales reason attached. A single foreign-key column on the fact table could only ever hold one of them.

The real fix is a dimension plus a bridge table — a table of order ID and reason key pairs that joins to the fact table through SalesOrderID, the degenerate dimension already sitting there. No new column goes on the fact table at all.

Because DimSalesReason and the bridge table are both brand new objects, nothing about the existing fact table or its four dimensions changes. Every query already built against this warehouse keeps working exactly as it did.
Next chapter builds the automated Python layer that validates this warehouse every time it refreshes, catching exactly these kinds of problems before any of the three front-ends ever sees them.
